title: Harvest and Bell
premise: Folklorist Xanthe Lockridge arrives in the frost-bound village of Harrow's Bell to record its carols, only to find the villagers refuse to sing any song twice — because the second singing is an answer, and something beneath the frozen orchard answers back. His sleep recordings reveal a second voice that knows his dead mother's lullabies, and as the frost patterns spread toward the church door he realizes the founders' unfinished ritual requires a singer who doesn't believe: him. Xanthe must choose between the skeptical isolation that has defined his life and the ragtag found family of villagers who teach him the final verse, completing the ritual at the winter solstice and laying the orchard-thing to rest — though the last recording suggests it left a seed of itself in his voice.
about_author: Q. M. Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist of regional folk music who spent a decade collecting field recordings across northern farming communities. They write horror about the places where tradition becomes obligation and songs become contracts.

chapters.title: The Bus That Only Runs in Winter
chapters.summary: Xanthe Lockridge arrives in Harrow's Bell with recording equipment and professional detachment, noting the village's strange silence and the frost patterns no one will discuss. Innkeeper Bess Marrow gives him a room and a warning. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Songs You Don't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: At the tavern, Xanthe coaxes old Tam Hollis into singing a harvest wassail; when asked for a second verse, the room goes cold and Tam leaves without paying. Bess explains nothing but locks the doors early. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: first crack in his skepticism.

chapters.title: Field Notes from a Frozen Orchard
chapters.summary: Xanthe explores the abandoned orchard where the founders supposedly planted their first trees, finding frost patterns arranged like musical notation on the bark. He records ambient sound; playback reveals a faint hum beneath the wind. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: scholarly excitement shading into unease.

chapters.title: Bess Keeps the Ledger
chapters.summary: Bess shows Xanthe the inn's founding ledger, its final pages filled with names crossed out each winter since 1847. She admits the village 'pays' something every solstice but refuses to say what. POV: Bess. Emotional beat: protective guilt.

chapters.title: What the Microphone Hears at Night
chapters.summary: Reviewing overnight recordings, Xanthe discovers a second voice answering questions he never asked aloud — including one in his mother's cadence. He tells himself it's interference. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: denial hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Choir That Won't Rehearse
chapters.summary: Xanthe attends the village choir, hoping to document the carols; the conductor, Reverend Ilsa Crane, halts rehearsal when two singers harmonize on the same verse twice. One chorister, young Wren, whispers to Xanthe that she wants to know why too. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: conspiratorial kinship beginning.

chapters.title: Wren's Questions
chapters.summary: Wren, orphaned and raised by the village collectively, shows Xanthe her own secret: frost patterns she's been sketching since childhood that match the orchard bark exactly. Neither of them can explain how she knows them. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the thrill of finally being believed.

chapters.title: The Founders' Hymnal
chapters.summary: In the church archive, Xanthe finds the founders' hymnal with the final pages torn out and a note: 'The last verse is sung, not written.' Reverend Crane catches him and orders him out, more frightened than angry. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the story becoming personal.

chapters.title: Second Voice
chapters.summary: The sleep recordings now capture full conversations: the second voice sings fragments of the missing verses and calls Xanthe 'the unbaptized ear.' His skepticism frays when it recites a lullaby only his mother knew. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: terror of being known.

chapters.title: Tam's Confession
chapters.summary: Drunk and desperate, Tam Hollis tells Xanthe the truth: the founders made a bargain with something in the orchard for a harvest that never fails, sealed in song, and every winter someone 'goes quiet.' His brother went quiet eleven years ago. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into warning.

chapters.title: The Frost Writes Its Pattern
chapters.summary: Overnight the frost reaches the inn's doorstep, forming the same notation across Bess's windows. The village holds an emergency meeting Xanthe isn't invited to; Wren sneaks him in through the cellar. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against taboo.

chapters.title: The Village Decides
chapters.summary: The elders vote to give the orchard what it asks: a singer who doesn't believe, meaning Xanthe. Bess votes no, alone. Xanthe, overhearing, understands he was recruited, not welcomed — or so he believes until Bess finds him shaking. POV: Bess. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into unexpected tenderness.

chapters.title: What Bess Buried Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Bess reveals her own history: her daughter went quiet nine winters ago, and Bess has kept the girl's recordings — which contain the same second voice. The thing has been learning Xanthe's mother tongue all along. POV: Bess. Emotional beat: shared mourning forging real family.

chapters.title: Reading the Notation
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Wren decode the frost notation using the hymnal's surviving pages: it's not a summons but half a ritual — the founders' binding, interrupted mid-verse. Finishing it could free the village; singing it wrong could feed the thing forever. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: purpose replacing fear.

chapters.title: Reverend Crane's Silence
chapters.summary: Crane confesses she tore out the hymnal's ending years ago to protect the village from temptation, believing containment safer than completion. Her silence has cost three lives. She surrenders the hidden pages. POV: Crane. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into repentance.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for the End of the World
chapters.summary: In the locked inn cellar, the unlikely ensemble — Xanthe, Wren, Bess, Tam, Crane — rehearses the completed ritual, their voices failing and mending together. The second voice listens from the recordings, growing impatient. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: found family harmonizing literally and figuratively.

chapters.title: The Night the Songs Stop
chapters.summary: Solstice eve: every bell, bird, and breath in Harrow's Bell goes silent. The frost climbs the church walls. The thing takes Tam's voice mid-rehearsal as payment for their delay, proving time has run out. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: sacrifice igniting resolve.

chapters.title: Into the Orchard
chapters.summary: The five walk into the frozen orchard at midnight, following the notation glowing in the ice. The thing wears the voices of everyone who 'went quiet,' including Bess's daughter and Xanthe's mother, offering each of them their deepest belonging if they stop singing. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: temptation at its most intimate.

chapters.title: The Verse That Isn't Written
chapters.summary: At the oldest tree, the ritual falters — the final verse must be invented, sung true, by the one who doesn't believe. Xanthe, voice breaking, sings not a spell but a promise: that he stays, that this is home. The others join. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: belief arriving sideways, through love rather than faith.

chapters.title: Harvest and Bell
chapters.summary: The binding completes: the frost notation collapses into ordinary snow, the orchard trees bloom black and bare, and the stolen voices release — Tam's returning hoarse but whole, Bess's daughter's fading with something like gratitude. The bell rings once, unstruck. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: awe and release.

chapters.title: The Second Singing
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the village sings the wassail twice freely, laughing at the old fear. Xanthe decides to stay, taking the archivist's room at the inn; Wren begins training as his apprentice. The family holds. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: belonging earned and chosen.

chapters.title: Appendix: Last Field Recording
chapters.summary: Epilogue as transcript: Xanthe's final archived recording captures him humming the new verse alone — and beneath it, faintly, a second voice humming harmony, patient, unhurried, waiting to be taught the words. POV: none (document). Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by one unresolved note.
